strings.name: Agnès Callamard
strings.role: Human-rights researcher · Amnesty International secretary general
strings.summary: Callamard moved from political science and refugee research into international human-rights work, leading Article 19 and Columbia’s freedom-of-expression project. As UN special rapporteur on extrajudicial executions from 2016 to 2021, she investigated cases including Jamal Khashoggi’s killing and called for further criminal accountability. She has led Amnesty International since 2021, engaging in free-expression, women’s-rights and global policy debates.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; reviewed on 15 November. This is not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Served as a UN special rapporteur and leads Amnesty International, contributing to accountability for unlawful killings and global human-rights policy discussions.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Grenoble political-studies degree (1985), Howard master’s (1988), political-science PhD at the New School (1995).
strings.highlights.h1.title: Unlawful-killing investigations
strings.highlights.h1.text: As an independent rapporteur investigated extrajudicial killings and sought further criminal investigation of the Khashoggi case.
strings.highlights.h2.title: International advocacy
strings.highlights.h2.text: Advanced free expression and human-rights protection at Article 19, Columbia and Amnesty.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Became Amnesty secretary general
strings.timeline.t1.text: Returned to Amnesty to lead its international secretariat and human-rights advocacy.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Published Khashoggi inquiry
strings.timeline.t2.text: Reported credible evidence warranting further investigation of senior officials’ possible responsibility; not a criminal verdict.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Became UN special rapporteur
strings.timeline.t3.text: Appointed to the extrajudicial, summary or arbitrary executions mandate, serving until 2021.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Led expression project
strings.timeline.t4.text: Became director of Columbia’s Global Freedom of Expression project.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Led Article 19
strings.timeline.t5.text: Began leading the free-expression organization Article 19, until 2013.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Founded accountability initiative
strings.timeline.t6.text: Became founding director of the Humanitarian Accountability Partnership, promoting aid-agency accountability.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Worked at Amnesty
strings.timeline.t7.text: Served as chef de cabinet and research-policy coordinator.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Earned political-science PhD
strings.timeline.t8.text: Completed refugee-focused doctoral research at the New School in New York.
